lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ل/ي/ل   l–y–l night, night‐time, 1 night, to enter night‐time.

Of this root, 4 forms occur 92 times in the Qur’an:
اللَيْل ʾal‐layl 74 times; لَيْل layl 5 times; لَيْلَةٌ laylatun 9 times and لَيَالِي layālı 4 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
لَيْلَةٌ laylatun [fem. n., pl. لَيَالِي layālı] a night

(44:3) إِنَّا‏ ‏أَنْزَلْنَاهُ‏ ‏فِي‏ ‏لَيْلَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ‏‏ We have sent it down on a blessed night!; *

(97:1) لَيْلَةُ القَدْر (see القَدْ ر ʾal‐qadr); *

(89:2) لَيَالٍ‏ ‏عَشْرٍ‏ layālin ʿashr [ten nights]. Opinions differ as to the meaning of this: the last ten days of the month of رَمَضَان Ramaḍān (in which لَيْلَةُ القَدْر laylatu’l‐qadr (q.v.), may fall, the first ten days of the month of ذُوالحِجَّة dhū’l‐˘ijjati during which the pilgrimage takes place, or the first ten days of the month of المُحَرَّم ʾal‐Muḥarram, which is the first month in the Islamic calendar.

entries.label: اللَيْل
entries.definitionHtml:
اللَيْل ʾal‐layl [n.]

1 night as opposed to day

(41:37) وَمِنْ‏ ‏ءَايَاتِهِ‏ ‏اللَّيْلُ‏ ‏وَالنَّهَارُ ‏‏وَالشَّمْسُ‏ ‏وَالْقَمَرُ‏ and of His signs‏ are the night and the day, the sun and the moon

(6:76) فَلَمَّا‏ ‏جَنَّ‏ ‏عَلَيْهِ‏ ‏اللَّيْلُ‏ ‏رَأَى كَوْكَبًا‏‏ when the night grew dark above him he saw a star

(73:2) قُمِ‏ ‏اللَّيْلَ‏ ‏إِلاَّ‏ ‏قَلِيلا‏ keep vigil throughout the night, all but a small part of it.
